sector: Healthcare (drug/pharmaceutical distribution chain: manufacturer, custodian, wholesaler-distributor, pharmacies)
hitl_conditions: Human keeps final say on recommendations in the online DT phase; caution required before redeploying a retrained agent; in the experiment recommendations are always followed automatically (no human). No explicit triggers for changing the human role.
key_finding: A two-phase framework trains a DRL agent (Dueling DDQN, action branching) in a simulated environment that then serves as the supply chain digital twin, recommending replenishment orders for a four-echelon drug chain; the agent approaches and sometimes exceeds base-stock performance, far exceeds a human-like heuristic, but is less stable.

quotes.text: This paper proposes a framework of a supply chain digital twin where decisions are taken by a DRL agent.
The Agent is used to recommend actions based on the digital twin. It is up to the decision-maker to follow the recommendations or not.
In this step, the Environment actually becomes an equivalent to the digital twin and the Agent replaces the human in charge of evaluating the different possibilities.
quotes.section: 3.2. Step 2: using the Environment as the digital twin (PDF p. 4 / p. 2294)

quotes.text: (i) Pharmaceutical establishments who manufacture, import and sell drugs, (ii) Custodians who distribute drugs, (iii) Wholesaler-distributors who resell drugs to pharmacies and (iv) Pharmacies or Internal pharmacies who act as retailers, respectively outside and inside hospitals.
It uses an architecture called Dueling Double Deep Q-Network (Dueling DDQN), taken from [36]. A Deep Q-Network (DQN) progressively learns the value of taking an action in a given state [37].
To evaluate the Agent’s performance, we simulate 100 episodes of 30 periods, where we will always follow its recommended actions. During evaluation, the Agent can no longer learn.
